tools.name: asset_search
tools.title: Search assets

display.title: Loopcut cloud asset library
display.summary: Search a hosted library of free models, materials and HDRIs.

tools.description: Finds existing models, materials, HDRIs or textures, including public Blender remote asset libraries, using query, source, license and size filters, with licence and credit attached. Use it to discover reusable assets. Searches are free, return at most 50 results and usually take 1–10 seconds; license any currently searches the same CC0 sources. The report attaches to the model; import selected results with existing asset tools or direct downloads.

kind.description: Asset category to search: one kind, a list of kinds, or any for every kind. Defaults to model.

limit.description: Maximum number of search results. Defaults to 10.

query.description: Search terms describing the desired asset; at most 1000 characters.

license.description: License filter. Defaults to cc0; any currently returns the same CC0 sources.

sources.description: Libraries to search. Defaults to all.

max_polycount.description: Maximum source-stated polygon count, for models only; ignored for other kinds. Assets with no stated polycount are excluded when set. Defaults to no cap.

min_resolution.description: Minimum longest side in pixels of the largest texture, HDRI or model texture set offered by the source. Assets with no stated resolution are excluded when set. Defaults to no minimum.

tools.name: auto_rig
tools.title: Rig humanoid

display.title: Auto-rig
display.summary: Add a skeleton and skin weights to a humanoid character.

tools.description: Adds a humanoid skeleton and skin weights to an uploaded GLB character. Use it for an unrigged human-shaped mesh with clearly separated limbs, not creatures, props or retargeting an existing animation; creatures are planned later. GLBs are limited to 100 MB and rig_type is humanoid only in v0; processing usually takes 1–5 minutes. Applying the result imports the rigged model and armature into the scene.

rig_type.description: Skeleton type. Defaults to humanoid, the only supported type in v0; creatures are planned later.

tools.name: dialogue_from_recordings
tools.title: Dialogue from recordings

display.title: Dialogue from your recordings
display.summary: Match your recorded takes to script lines and place them on the timeline.

tools.description: Matches recorded takes to speaker-labelled script lines and returns cleaned dialogue audio plus a matching report. Use it to assemble an existing performance, not to invent missing words or synthesize a voice; it remains available with generation off. A recording bundle and quote are required, and processing usually takes a few minutes per recorded minute, depending on cleanup and the number of takes. Applying the result adds one audio strip per matched line to the sequencer and attaches the report of matches and gaps.

bundle_input.description: Bundle of raw recording takes in WAV or MP3 format, referenced by a bundle manifest; the script is supplied separately in input. Include the recording blobs as bundle members.

script.description: Script lines with speaker names, for example Ada: Hello. The recordings must contain the requested lines; at most 100000 characters.

language.description: BCP-47 language tag, for example en-US or fr-FR. Defaults to en-US; supported languages depend on the route.

tools.name: image_edit
tools.title: Edit image

display.title: Image editing
display.summary: Change an existing image or render with a text instruction.

tools.description: Changes an existing image from a text instruction, including restyling a render or changing a selected area. Use a mask for a local change; use image generation for a new composition and scene tools for exact geometry changes. The source is required and source/mask uploads are limited to 50 MB each; an optional PNG alpha mask must match its dimensions, with transparent pixels marking the area to edit, and edits usually take 15–90 seconds. Applying the result adds an image reference to the scene.

size.description: Output width and height in pixels. Defaults to 1024x1024.

prompt.description: Describe the changes to make and the features to preserve; at most 4000 characters.

quality.description: Image detail and compute budget. Defaults to medium; high (HD) costs 20 credits versus 6 for low or medium, at any size.

tools.name: image_generate
tools.title: Generate image

display.title: Image generation
display.summary: Create a reference image or backplate from a text prompt.

tools.description: Creates a still image from a prompt, optionally guided by a reference image. Use it for concept art, backplates or visual references; use image editing to change an existing image and a 3D tool for geometry. Prompts are limited to 4000 characters and reference images to 20 MB; results usually take 15–90 seconds. Applying the result adds an image reference to the scene.

size.description: Output width and height in pixels. Defaults to 1024x1024.

prompt.description: Describe the subject, composition, lighting and visual style; at most 4000 characters.

quality.description: Image detail and compute budget. Defaults to medium; high (HD) costs 20 credits versus 6 for low or medium, at any size.

background.description: Output background treatment. Defaults to opaque; transparent produces a PNG with alpha.

tools.name: image_to_3d
tools.title: Image to 3D model

display.title: Image to 3D
display.summary: Turn an image or a description into a textured 3D model.

tools.description: Creates a GLB mesh with PBR materials from an image, a prompt or both; at least one of image and prompt is required. Use it for a new prop or concept mesh, not dimensionally exact CAD or cleanup of an existing mesh. Drafts cost 25 credits and finals 80, usually taking 1–5 minutes; hidden surfaces are inferred and quads do not guarantee animation-ready edge flow. Applying the result imports the model and its materials into the scene.

prompt.description: Describe the object to generate. Optional when an image file is supplied; otherwise required, at most 1024 characters.

quality.description: Generation detail. Defaults to final (80 credits); draft costs 25 credits.

textured.description: Include PBR materials and textures. Defaults to true; false returns geometry only.

topology.description: Preferred face topology. Defaults to triangles; quads are a target rather than a guarantee of clean edge flow.

tools.name: lip_sync
tools.title: Lip sync audio

display.title: Lip sync
display.summary: Animate a character's existing mouth shapes from a speech recording.

tools.description: Creates mouth animation curves from an existing speech recording for a mesh with viseme shape keys. Use it to synchronize a prepared face to recorded dialogue, not to generate speech, create missing shape keys or rig a face. Audio must be WAV or MP3 up to 100 MB; processing usually takes seconds to a few minutes per recorded minute and requires the target mesh’s existing viseme names. Applying the result animates those shape keys on the target mesh at the requested frame rate.

fps.description: Animation frames per second, including fractional rates such as 29.97. Defaults to 24.

items.description: An existing viseme shape-key name on the target mesh.

shape_keys.description: Names of the target mesh’s existing viseme shape keys. Required; 1–64 unique names.

tools.name: motion_from_text
tools.title: Motion from text

display.title: Motion from text
display.summary: Make a character animation from a short description of an action.

in_place.description: Keep the pelvis over its starting position, so the character animates without travelling (for loops and game clips). Defaults to false.

target_armature.description: Name of the armature object in the open scene to put the motion on: a Mixamo, Rigify, Auto-Rig Pro, Unreal mannequin or other humanoid rig. Omit it to use the active or the only selected humanoid armature; with none, the motion is imported on its own skeleton with a simple body.

tools.description: Generates a humanoid body animation from a short description of one action, with NVIDIA Kimodo (built with Meta Llama 3). Use it for walks, runs, jumps, gestures, dances and other full-body actions, not facial animation, finger work, holding props or interacting with objects; the fingers stay still. One action per prompt, at most 400 characters, and 2–10 seconds of motion; it costs 2 credits per second of motion, rounded up to whole seconds, and takes under a minute, or a few minutes when the service starts cold. Applying the result retargets the motion onto target_armature (or the selected humanoid armature) or, with none, imports it on its own skeleton with a simple body; in_place keeps it from travelling.

seed.description: Optional random seed; the same prompt, length and seed give the same motion. Omit it for a new variation each run.

prompt.description: One action in plain words, e.g. "a person walks forward four steps, stops and waves with the right hand"; at most 400 characters.

duration_s.description: Length of the motion in seconds, 2–10. Defaults to 5.

tools.name: motion_from_video
tools.title: Motion from video

display.title: Motion from video
display.summary: Capture a person's movement from a video and put it on your character's rig.

in_place.description: Keep the pelvis over its starting position, so the character animates without travelling (for loops and game clips). Defaults to false.

target_armature.description: Name of the armature object in the open scene to put the motion on: a Mixamo, Rigify, Auto-Rig Pro, Unreal mannequin or other humanoid rig. Omit it to use the active or the only selected humanoid armature; with none, the motion is imported on its own skeleton with a simple body.

tools.description: Captures a person's full-body motion, hands included, from a video, with NVIDIA GEM-X. Use it to turn the user's own performance or a reference clip into animation, not to generate motion from words. Works best with one person, the whole body in view, a mostly still camera and good light; first-person views, gloved or hidden hands, heavy occlusion and fast spins track poorly. The video must be MP4, MOV or WebM up to 200 MB, and the captured part at most 60 seconds (choose it with start_s and end_s); it costs 3 credits per second of video captured, rounded up to whole seconds with a 2-second minimum, quoted first, and takes one to a few minutes. Applying the result retargets the motion onto target_armature (or the selected humanoid armature) or, with none, imports it on its own skeleton with a simple body; in_place keeps it from travelling.

end_s.description: Second of the video where the capture ends, at most 60 seconds after start_s. Defaults to the end of the video.

start_s.description: Second of the video where the capture starts. Defaults to 0.

static_camera.description: True when the camera does not move (a tripod shot); it steadies the character's path through the scene. Defaults to false.

video_seconds.description: Length of the uploaded video in seconds, as the client measured it. The quote and the capture cover at most this much; omitted, the quote holds the 60-second maximum and the charge is the seconds actually captured (2 seconds at least).

tools.name: render
tools.title: Render scene

display.title: Cloud rendering
display.summary: Render your scene on cloud GPUs and get the frames back.

tools.description: Renders the bundled Blender scene with Cycles or EEVEE on cloud GPUs and returns frames plus a QA report. Use it for final stills, frame ranges or a 360° turntable of an existing scene, not image generation or an interactive viewport preview. Render with the scene's own engine: pass engine "eevee" for a scene set to EEVEE. A self-contained scene bundle and a quote are required, and it costs 5 credits per GPU-minute with a one-minute minimum; render time ranges from minutes to hours depending on scene complexity, frame count and samples. Applying the result loads the frames and attaches the QA report.

bundle_input.description: Self-contained Blender scene bundle: entry is a .blend file, with all textures, linked libraries, caches and other external dependencies collected at relative paths. Member MIME types are unrestricted to support scene dependencies.

camera.description: Name of the scene camera object. If omitted, use the active camera in the bundle.

engine.description: Render engine. Use the scene's own: "eevee" when scene.render.engine is BLENDER_EEVEE. Defaults to "cycles".

denoise.description: Denoise rendered frames (Cycles; EEVEE ignores it). Defaults to true.

samples.description: Samples per pixel: Cycles samples, or EEVEE render samples. Defaults to 128 for Cycles and 64 for EEVEE.

frame_end.description: Last frame to render, inclusive; must be at least frame_start. Defaults to frame_start for a single frame, or 120 frames for a turntable.

margin.description: Framing padding; 1 fits the targets' bounding sphere exactly. Defaults to 1.15.

targets.description: Objects to frame and orbit, usually the selection; their children are included. Empty or omitted frames the whole scene.

elevation_deg.description: Camera height as an angle above the targets' centre. Defaults to 20.

turntable.description: Render a 360° turntable instead of the scene camera: a generated camera orbits the target objects (or the whole scene) once across frame_start..frame_end, so the frames loop seamlessly. If frame_end is omitted, renders 120 frames. A named camera only lends its lens.

frame_step.description: Spacing between rendered frames. Defaults to 1.

frame_start.description: First frame to render, inclusive. Defaults to 1.

resolution_pct.description: Percentage of the scene output resolution. Defaults to 100.

tools.name: retopology
tools.title: Retopologize model

display.title: Retopology
display.summary: Rebuild a dense mesh with cleaner, lighter topology.

tools.description: Rebuilds an existing GLB mesh with clean quad or triangle topology, unwraps it and bakes the original's textures (base colour, normal, roughness and metallic) onto the new mesh. Typical target_faces by purpose: about 2000–5000 for a game prop or background asset, 5000–10000 for an editing or sculpting base, 10000–20000 for a hero asset or character. Without target_faces the service chooses from the source, about half its triangle count within 4000–16000 quads. It does not generate new objects or guarantee deformation-ready edge loops. Input GLBs are limited to 150 MB; the current route supports up to 20000 quads or 40000 triangles, and processing usually takes under two minutes. It usually costs 5 credits (up to 60 on the backup route), never more than the quote. Applying the result imports a new mesh into the scene.

topology.description: Preferred output face topology. Defaults to quads.

target_faces.description: Output face count, 500–200000; the current route supports up to 20000 quads or 40000 triangles. Omit it to let the service choose from the source. By purpose: game prop or background asset 2000–5000, editing or sculpting base 5000–10000, hero asset or character 10000–20000.

tools.name: sfx
tools.title: Generate sound effect

display.title: Sound effects
display.summary: Create a sound effect from a short description.

tools.description: Creates a sound effect from a description, with optional seamless looping. Use it for impacts, ambience or foley, not spoken dialogue, music or editing a recorded sound. Duration is limited to 0.5–30 seconds; most effects take 5–30 seconds; a take up to 6 seconds costs 4 credits, plus 1 credit per extra 2 seconds. Applying the result adds an audio strip to the sequencer.

loop.description: Make the start and end join for repeated playback. Defaults to false.

prompt.description: Describe the sound source, action, environment and acoustic character; at most 4000 characters.

duration_seconds.description: Length of the effect in seconds. Defaults to 2; accepted range is 0.5–30.

tools.name: voice_line
tools.title: Generate voice line

display.title: Voice lines
display.summary: Turn written lines into spoken audio for your scene.

tools.description: Creates spoken audio from text with a selectable voice and performance direction. Use it for character lines or narration, not music, sound effects, voice cloning or cleaning a recorded performance. Text is limited to 2000 characters; a short line usually takes 5–30 seconds, at 10 credits per minute of speech, rounded up per line with a 1-credit minimum. Applying the result adds an audio strip to the sequencer.

text.description: Words to speak; at most 2000 characters.

voice.description: Voice character: Zephyr (bright), Puck (upbeat), Charon (informative), Kore (firm), Fenrir (excitable), Leda (youthful), Aoede (breezy), Sulafat (warm). Defaults to Kore.

language.description: BCP-47 language tag, for example en-US or fr-FR. Defaults to en-US; supported languages depend on the route.

direction.description: Performance direction such as tone, pace and emotion; at most 1000 characters. If omitted, use a neutral delivery.
